peers.name: CENTRAL MINE P N D INST L

profile.entities: Dhruv Consultancy Services Limited; Dhruv UK Subsidiary; Mozambique Branch
profile.subseg: Highways; Bridges; Airports; Railways; Urban Infrastructure
profile.themes: Sectoral Diversification; International Expansion; Digital Transformation; State Government Project Capture

bull_bear.body: Reinvestment in talent acquisition, digital capabilities (BIM/AI), and international business development; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on organic growth via empanelments and JV partnerships
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Dependence on government payments (though 100% guaranteed); slow international project conversion cycles (2-year lead time); bid win rate currently low at 1% abroad (targeting 5-10%); potential delays in land acquisition affecting certification and cash flow
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, proactive, and strategically focused; management emphasizes recovery from debarment, sectoral diversification, and digital transformation; tone is optimistic on Q3/Q4 performance and international pipeline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite 90% order book from NHAI, management is actively reducing dependency by targeting state governments with higher margins; international revenue potential is underappreciated — Mozambique project already delivered, with Ghana/Zambia in advanced talks; BIM/AI adoption is not just efficiency play but a competitive moat for winning larger global tenders
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Revenue mix: 80% PMC (incl. O&M & construction supervision), 20% DPR; O&M: 40% of revenue; Construction supervision: 40%; DPR: 20%; New verticals: aviation (MIHAN INR1.63cr), traffic census (PWD empanelment), railways (3 projects), metros (4 MMRDA projects)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NHAI debarment caused 40% revenue drop in Q2FY26 | DHRUV | beneficiary | High | Debarment lifted in July 2025; recent empanelments and bid wins confirm recovery |
| Low international bid win rate (1%) | DHRUV | beneficiary | Medium | Targeting 5-10% win rate; Africa pipeline is active and JV model is proven |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin compressed in H1 due to debarment and lower certification delays; targeting 30-35% in new sectors (aviation, metros); cost control maintained via low attrition (3-4%) and in-house talent pool; USD-denominated international contracts improve margin resilience
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Q3/Q4 to outperform H1; Margin: targeting 30-35% in new sectors (aviation, metros); Order inflow: INR70-80cr expected by end of Q4FY26 from current INR250cr bid pipeline; Capex/Commissioning: none planned; digital tools implementation ongoing
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR200 crores unexecuted, to be executed over 2.5-3 years; 90% from NHAI/MoRTH, rest from MSIDC, CIDCO, MADC, OBCC
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: International expansion in Africa (Ghana, Zambia, Tanzania, Cambodia) and Southeast Asia; potential for large-ticket airport projects (INR10-15cr each); state government projects (INR25cr+ ticket size); BIM/AI adoption enabling higher project throughput
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Dhruv has recovered from a temporary NHAI debarment and is accelerating growth through strategic empanelments in high-margin state and aviation infrastructure, with a clear shift from central to state-led projects and international bids in Africa and Southeast Asia, positioning it for margin expansion beyond traditional highway dependency.

meta.thesis: Dhruv has recovered from a temporary NHAI debarment and is accelerating growth through strategic empanelments in high-margin state and aviation infrastructure, with a clear shift from central to state-led projects and international bids in Africa and Southeast Asia, positioning it for margin expansion beyond traditional highway dependency.
